```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)

```

# Model and source

McCarthy 2026 compared the predictive performance of published vancomycin
population PK models in two US multi-site routine-care data sets: paediatric
oncology patients (Study 1) and paediatric cardiovascular intensive care unit
(CVICU) patients (Study 2). It then re-estimated the best-performing models on
its own data. Those three re-estimated ("refit") models are the models in this
package; the published originals they started from are separate papers.

| Model | Structure | Refit data | Source |
|-------|-----------|------------|--------|
| `McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_colin` | Colin 2019 (Onc), 2-compartment | 371 oncology + 371 matched non-oncology patients | Table 4; Supplementary file 2 |
| `McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_moffett` | Moffett 2019, 1-compartment | 219 CVICU patients | Table 5; Supplementary file 2 |
| `McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_shimamoto` | Shimamoto 2024, 2-compartment | 219 CVICU patients | Table 6; Supplementary file 2 |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_shimamoto"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01623-7> (open access, PMC13038739)

Supplementary file 2 prints the complete NONMEM control stream of every
evaluated model, including the three refits with their final `$THETA`,
`$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` estimates. The model files transcribe those streams;
Tables 4 to 6 give the same estimates rounded to two decimals.

The refit Shimamoto 2024 model performed best overall in the CVICU patients.
In the oncology patients the re-estimated cancer-status effect (0.06) was
indistinguishable from zero, and the refit did not improve on the published
Colin 2019 model.

```{r models}
mod_colin <- readModelDb("McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_colin")
mod_moffett <- readModelDb("McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_moffett")
mod_shimamoto <- readModelDb("McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_shimamoto")
```

# Population

Patients under 20 years treated with intermittent intravenous vancomycin and
entered into the InsightRX Nova dosing software between January 2018 and
April 2025 (Methods; Table 1). Patients on haemodialysis, CRRT, ECMO or a
ventricular assist device, or tagged as NICU or PICU patients, were excluded.

* **Study 1 (Colin refit).** 371 oncology patients from 20 sites (82%
  haematological malignancy, 3.2% solid tumour, 15% unspecified; 13%
  neutropenic) and 371 propensity-score matched non-oncology patients. Median
  age 7.2 and 7.9 years (range 0.2-20.0), median weight 26 and 28 kg (range
  5-124), median serum creatinine 0.35 and 0.34 mg/dL. 1392 + 1257 vancomycin
  concentrations.
* **Study 2 (Moffett and Shimamoto refits).** 219 CVICU patients from 11 sites,
  46% female, median age 1.1 years (range 0.1-17.8), median postmenstrual age
  99 weeks (range 46-970), median weight 9 kg (range 3-91), median serum
  creatinine 0.31 mg/dL (range 0.06-2.44); 1136 concentrations. The matched
  non-CVICU controls were not used in the refits.

Each treatment course was treated as a separate individual in NONMEM. Race
and ethnicity were not reported. The same information is available from each
model's `population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("McCarthy_2026_vancomycin_shimamoto")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. "CS" is
the refit NONMEM control stream in Supplementary file 2.

| Model | Parameter | Value | Source location |
|-------|-----------|-------|-----------------|
| Colin | `lcl`, `lvc`, `lvp`, `lq` | 1.51077, 3.57148, 3.9105, 0.807181 (log scale) | Table 4 refit 1.51, 3.57, 3.91, 0.81; CS `$THETA(1)`-`(4)` |
| Colin | `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | CS `(V1/RV1)**0.75`, `(V2/RV2)**0.75`; Table S2 |
| Colin | `ltdec50`, `ltmat50`, `lhill_mat`, `lhill_dec`, `le_creat_cl` | 4.12, -0.113, 1.06, 0.807, -0.433 (fixed, log scale) | CS `$THETA(5)`-`(9)` FIX (Colin 2019 values) |
| Colin | `e_cancer_ped_cl` | 0.0563011 | Table 4 refit thetaCANC 0.06; CS `$THETA(12)` |
| Colin | `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalvp` | 0.0652814, 0.171886, 0.862485 | CS `$OMEGA`; Table 4 omega 0.26, 0.41, 0.93 (square roots) |
| Colin | `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.2226, 0.8052 | sqrt of CS `$SIGMA` 0.0495662, 0.648283; Table 4 0.22, 0.81 |
| Colin | maturation, decline, standardised creatinine | equations | CS `$PK` (`Fmat`, `Fage`, `LnSCRstd`, `Fscr`) |
| Moffett | `lcl`, `lvc` | log(7.4986), log(70.4378) | Table 5 refit 7.50, 70.44; CS `$THETA(1)`-`(2)` |
| Moffett | `e_page_cl`, `tmat50` | -0.169922, 50 weeks (fixed) | Table 5 refit thetaPMA -0.17; CS `$THETA(3)`, `FMAT = 1/(1+(PMA/50)**THETA(3))` |
| Moffett | `e_crcl_cl`, `e_wt_cl` | 0.768862, 0.75 (fixed) | Table 5 refit thetaCRCL 0.77; CS `$THETA(4)`, `(WT/70)**0.75` |
| Moffett | `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.103392, 0.123482 | CS `$OMEGA`; Table 5 omega 0.32, 0.35 |
| Moffett | `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.238867, 0.0001 (fixed) | Table 5 refit thetaPROP 0.24; CS `$THETA(5)`, `$THETA(6)` FIX |
| Moffett | `crcl` | `0.413 * HT / CREAT` | CS `$PK` |
| Shimamoto | `lcl`, `lvc`, `lvp` | log(3.56332), log(12.7238), log(26.7204) | Table 6 refit 3.56, 12.72, 26.72; CS `$THETA(1)`, `(2)`, `(4)` |
| Shimamoto | `lq`, `hill_mat`, `tmat50` | log(2.95), 1.73, 36.9 weeks (fixed) | Table 6 published values (refit blank); CS `$THETA(3)`, `(6)`, `(7)` FIX |
| Shimamoto | `e_wt_cl`, `e_crcl_cl`, `e_wt_q` | 0.559713, 0.630524, 0.75 (fixed) | Table 6 refit thetaWT 0.56, thetaCRCL 0.63; CS `$THETA(10)`, `(5)`, `(WT/70)**0.75` |
| Shimamoto | `etalcl`, `etalvp` | 0.068973, 0.217882 | CS `$OMEGA`; Table 6 omega 0.26, 0.47 |
| Shimamoto | `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.207734, 0.890438 | Table 6 refit 0.21, 0.89; CS `$THETA(8)`, `(9)` |
| Shimamoto | `crcl` with age-banded `k_schwartz` | 0.244 / 0.277 / 0.296 / 0.413 | CS `$PK` ('eGFR calculated by revised Schwartz') |

# Typical values against Tables 4 to 6

Tables 4 to 6 print the refit estimates to two decimals and the IIV as the
square root of the `$OMEGA` variance. The check below rebuilds each printed
number from the packaged `ini()` values.

```{r typical-values}
ini_value <- function(mod, name) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
  ie <- ui$iniDf
  row <- ie[!is.na(ie$name) & ie$name == name, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("no unique ini() row for '", name, "'")
  row$est
}

typ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model, ~parameter, ~packaged, ~printed,
  "Colin", "thetaCL (log)", ini_value(mod_colin, "lcl"), 1.51,
  "Colin", "thetaVD1 (log)", ini_value(mod_colin, "lvc"), 3.57,
  "Colin", "thetaVD2 (log)", ini_value(mod_colin, "lvp"), 3.91,
  "Colin", "thetaQ2 (log)", ini_value(mod_colin, "lq"), 0.81,
  "Colin", "thetaCANC", ini_value(mod_colin, "e_cancer_ped_cl"), 0.06,
  "Colin", "thetaPROP", ini_value(mod_colin, "propSd"), 0.22,
  "Colin", "thetaADD", ini_value(mod_colin, "addSd"), 0.81,
  "Colin", "omegaCL", sqrt(ini_value(mod_colin, "etalcl")), 0.26,
  "Colin", "omegaVD1", sqrt(ini_value(mod_colin, "etalvc")), 0.41,
  "Colin", "omegaVD2", sqrt(ini_value(mod_colin, "etalvp")), 0.93,
  "Moffett", "thetaCL", exp(ini_value(mod_moffett, "lcl")), 7.50,
  "Moffett", "thetaVD", exp(ini_value(mod_moffett, "lvc")), 70.44,
  "Moffett", "thetaPMA", ini_value(mod_moffett, "e_page_cl"), -0.17,
  "Moffett", "thetaCRCL", ini_value(mod_moffett, "e_crcl_cl"), 0.77,
  "Moffett", "thetaPROP", ini_value(mod_moffett, "propSd"), 0.24,
  "Moffett", "omegaCL", sqrt(ini_value(mod_moffett, "etalcl")), 0.32,
  "Moffett", "omegaVD", sqrt(ini_value(mod_moffett, "etalvc")), 0.35,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaCL", exp(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "lcl")), 3.56,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaVD1", exp(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "lvc")), 12.72,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaQ", exp(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "lq")), 2.95,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaVD2", exp(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "lvp")), 26.72,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaWT", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "e_wt_cl"), 0.56,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaCRCL", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "e_crcl_cl"), 0.63,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaHILL", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "hill_mat"), 1.73,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaT50", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "tmat50"), 36.90,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaPROP", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "propSd"), 0.21,
  "Shimamoto", "thetaADD", ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "addSd"), 0.89,
  "Shimamoto", "omegaCL", sqrt(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "etalcl")), 0.26,
  "Shimamoto", "omegaVD2", sqrt(ini_value(mod_shimamoto, "etalvp")), 0.47
) |>
  mutate(`Rounded to 2 dp` = round(packaged, 2), Match = abs(`Rounded to 2 dp` - printed) < 1e-9)

# Every printed refit value is the packaged value rounded to two decimals.
stopifnot(nrow(typ) == 29L, all(typ$Match))

typ |>
  mutate(packaged = signif(packaged, 6)) |>
  rename(Model = model, Parameter = parameter, Packaged = packaged, `Table 4-6` = printed) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Packaged values against the refit columns of Tables 4 to 6.")
```

# Structural checks

## Colin: reference subject and standardised creatinine

The Colin structure normalises maturation and decline to a 35-year-old born at
40 weeks (`PMA_R = 35+(40/52)` years) and centres creatinine on an
age-standardised value; the control stream notes that this is 0.84 mg/dL for
the reference adult. A typical 70-kg reference subject whose creatinine equals
that standard must therefore have `CL = exp(lcl)` exactly. The cancer-status
effect multiplies CL by `1 + 0.0563`.

```{r colin-reference}
pma_ref_wk <- (35 + 40 / 52) * 52
creat_std_ref <- exp(-1.22839 + log10(35 + 40 / 52) * 0.67190 + 6.27017 * exp(-3.10940 * (35 + 40 / 52)))

ref_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  WT = 70, PAGE = pma_ref_wk, CREAT = creat_std_ref, DIS_CANCER_PED = c(0, 1)
)
# Typical-value solve: rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega.
ref_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_colin), events = ref_ev, returnType = "data.frame"))

colin_ref <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Standardised creatinine at the reference age (mg/dL)",
    "CL, reference subject, DIS_CANCER_PED = 0 (L/h)",
    "CL ratio, DIS_CANCER_PED = 1 vs 0"
  ),
  Model = c(ref_sim$creat_std[1], ref_sim$cl[1], ref_sim$cl[2] / ref_sim$cl[1]),
  Expected = c(0.84, exp(1.51077), 1 + 0.0563011)
)
stopifnot(
  # The stream comment states 0.84 to two decimals; the formula gives 0.831.
  abs(colin_ref$Model[1] / 0.84 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(colin_ref$Model[2] / colin_ref$Expected[2] - 1) < 1e-8,
  abs(colin_ref$Model[3] / colin_ref$Expected[3] - 1) < 1e-8
)
knitr::kable(colin_ref, digits = 4, caption = "Colin refit at the reference subject.")
```

## Shimamoto: age-banded Schwartz coefficient

```{r shimamoto-schwartz}
sch_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  AGE = c(0.2, 0.2, 5, 12, 15), WT = c(2.2, 4, 18, 40, 55),
  HT = c(45, 55, 108, 150, 165), CREAT = 0.4, PAGE = c(50, 50, 300, 664, 820)
)
# Typical-value solve: rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega.
sch_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_shimamoto), events = sch_ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
k_expected <- c(0.244, 0.277, 0.296, 0.413, 0.413)
stopifnot(max(abs(sch_sim$crcl / (k_expected * sch_ev$HT / sch_ev$CREAT) - 1)) < 1e-10)
sch_ev |>
  select(AGE, WT, HT, CREAT) |>
  mutate(k = k_expected, `CRCL (mL/min/1.73 m^2)` = round(sch_sim$crcl, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Creatinine clearance computed inside the Shimamoto refit for each Schwartz band.")
```

# Refit against published estimates

Tables 4 to 6 print the published estimate next to each refit estimate, and
the Results describe how they differ: for Moffett the refit volume and IIV were
higher and the PMA and CRCL effects weaker; for Shimamoto the refit CL, V1 and
weight exponent were lower and the CRCL effect stronger; for Colin the cancer
effect fell from 0.29 to 0.06. The figure shows the typical clearance of each
refit model and of the same structure carrying the published estimates (from
the published-model control streams in Supplementary file 2), for a typical
child of each age with serum creatinine 0.35 mg/dL.

```{r growth}
# Approximate median weight and height for age (CDC/WHO growth charts, both
# sexes); used only to build plausible covariate combinations.
growth <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age, ~wt, ~ht,
  0.00, 3.3, 50,
  0.25, 6.0, 61,
  0.50, 7.6, 67,
  1.00, 9.6, 75,
  2.00, 12.2, 87,
  3.00, 14.3, 96,
  5.00, 18.3, 110,
  7.00, 23.0, 122,
  10.00, 32.0, 138,
  13.00, 46.0, 156,
  15.00, 56.0, 167,
  18.00, 66.0, 175,
  20.00, 68.0, 176
)
wt_for_age <- function(age) stats::approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = age, rule = 2)$y
ht_for_age <- function(age) stats::approx(growth$age, growth$ht, xout = age, rule = 2)$y
```

```{r refit-vs-published, fig.height = 5}
ages <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10, 14, 18)
grid <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(ages), time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  AGE = ages, WT = wt_for_age(ages), HT = ht_for_age(ages),
  PAGE = ages * 52 + 40, CREAT = 0.35, DIS_CANCER_PED = 1
)

typical_cl <- function(mod, label, version) {
  # Typical-value solve: rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega.
  out <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = grid, returnType = "data.frame"))
  tibble::tibble(AGE = grid$AGE, cl = out$cl, model = label, version = version)
}

# Published estimates, from the published-model control streams in
# Supplementary file 2 (and the published columns of Tables 4 to 6).
colin_pub <- mod_colin |>
  rxode2::ini(lcl = 1.67, lvc = 3.75, lvp = 3.73, lq = 1.17, e_cancer_ped_cl = 0.294)
moffett_pub <- mod_moffett |>
  rxode2::ini(lcl = log(7.86), lvc = log(63.6), e_page_cl = -0.285, e_crcl_cl = 0.9)
shimamoto_pub <- mod_shimamoto |>
  rxode2::ini(lcl = log(4.88), lvc = log(21.6), lvp = log(21.7), e_wt_cl = 0.75, e_crcl_cl = 0.551)

cl_cmp <- bind_rows(
  typical_cl(mod_colin, "Colin 2019 (Onc), oncology patient", "Refit"),
  typical_cl(colin_pub, "Colin 2019 (Onc), oncology patient", "Published"),
  typical_cl(mod_moffett, "Moffett 2019", "Refit"),
  typical_cl(moffett_pub, "Moffett 2019", "Published"),
  typical_cl(mod_shimamoto, "Shimamoto 2024", "Refit"),
  typical_cl(shimamoto_pub, "Shimamoto 2024", "Published")
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(cl_cmp$cl), nrow(cl_cmp) == 6L * length(ages))

ggplot(cl_cmp, aes(AGE, cl / wt_for_age(AGE), colour = version)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)", y = "Typical clearance (L/h/kg)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical vancomycin clearance: refit vs published estimates",
    caption = "Refit estimates from Tables 4-6 of McCarthy 2026; published estimates from Supplementary file 2."
  )
```

```{r refit-vs-published-check}
ratio <- cl_cmp |>
  select(AGE, model, version, cl) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = version, values_from = cl) |>
  mutate(ratio = Refit / Published)

ratio_at <- function(m) ratio$ratio[ratio$model == m]
# Colin: with all other covariates equal, the refit / published CL ratio of an
# oncology patient is exp(1.51077 - 1.67) * (1.0563 / 1.294) at every age,
# because only CL, the cancer effect and the volumes (which cancel in V1/RV1)
# changed.
colin_expected <- exp(1.51077 - 1.67) * (1 + 0.0563011) / (1 + 0.294)
stopifnot(max(abs(ratio_at("Colin 2019 (Onc), oncology patient") / colin_expected - 1)) < 1e-8)
# Moffett and Shimamoto: the refit lowers typical CL in older children (weaker
# CRCL effect at CRCL above the reference for Moffett; lower thetaCL for
# Shimamoto), as Results 'Study 2: popPK Model Refitting' describes.
stopifnot(
  ratio_at("Moffett 2019")[length(ages)] < 1,
  ratio_at("Shimamoto 2024")[length(ages)] < 1
)
ratio |>
  mutate(ratio = round(ratio, 3)) |>
  select(model, AGE, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = ratio) |>
  rename(`Age (years)` = AGE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Refit / published typical clearance by age.")
```

# Virtual cohorts

The original data are not public. The cohorts below approximate Table 1:
age drawn log-normally around the reported median and inter-quartile range and
truncated to the reported range, weight and height from approximate growth
medians with between-child scatter, postmenstrual age as age plus 40 weeks
(the paper's own imputation for most patients), and serum creatinine
log-normal around the reported median. Each arm has 200 patients. All patients
receive 15 mg/kg as a 1-hour infusion, every 6 h in Study 1 and every 8 h in
Study 2, matching the median dose (428 mg for a median 26 kg; 125 mg for 9 kg)
and interval in Table 1, simulated at steady state.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)

# rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's draws for a given number of solver threads only;
# every assertion below holds for any cohort the models can produce.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

draw_age <- function(n, median, iqr, range) {
  sdlog <- diff(log(iqr)) / 1.349
  a <- exp(rnorm(n, log(median), sdlog))
  pmin(pmax(a, range[1]), range[2])
}

make_cohort <- function(n, cohort, age_med, age_iqr, age_range, tau, id_offset, cancer) {
  age <- draw_age(n, age_med, age_iqr, age_range)
  wt <- wt_for_age(age) * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.15))
  ht <- ht_for_age(age) * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.04))
  creat <- pmin(pmax(0.33 * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.4)), 0.06), 2.44)
  subj <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n), cohort = cohort, AGE = age, WT = wt, HT = ht,
    PAGE = age * 52 + 40, CREAT = creat, DIS_CANCER_PED = cancer, tau = tau,
    dose = 15 * wt
  )
  doses <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, rate = dose, ii = tau, ss = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs_times <- c(seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.05), seq(1.6, 8, by = 0.1))
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    filter(time <= tau) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

study1 <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200, "Oncology", 7.2, c(3.4, 13.3), c(0.2, 20), 6, 0L, 1),
  make_cohort(200, "Non-oncology", 7.9, c(3.9, 14.1), c(0.3, 18.4), 6, 200L, 0)
)
study2 <- make_cohort(200, "CVICU", 1.1, c(0.4, 5.2), c(0.1, 17.8), 8, 400L, 0)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(unique(study1[, c("id", "time", "evid")])),
  !anyDuplicated(unique(study2[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
)

study1 |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  bind_rows(distinct(study2, id, .keep_all = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(cohort) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(), `Age (y)` = median(AGE), `PMA (wk)` = median(PAGE), `Weight (kg)` = median(WT),
    `Height (cm)` = median(HT), `Creatinine (mg/dL)` = median(CREAT), `Dose (mg)` = median(dose),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohorts (medians); compare McCarthy 2026 Table 1.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
keep_cols <- c("cohort", "tau", "dose")
sim_colin <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_colin, events = study1, keep = keep_cols, maxsteps = 1e6,
  returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(model = "Colin refit")
sim_moffett <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_moffett, events = study2, keep = keep_cols, maxsteps = 1e6,
  returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(model = "Moffett refit")
sim_shimamoto <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_shimamoto, events = study2, keep = keep_cols, maxsteps = 1e6,
  returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(model = "Shimamoto refit")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_colin, sim_moffett, sim_shimamoto) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(model, cohort, sep = ": "))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

```{r profiles, fig.height = 5}
sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(15, 20), linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Vancomycin (mg/L)",
    title = "Steady-state profiles, 15 mg/kg as a 1-h infusion",
    caption = paste(
      "Median and 90% interval of individual predictions (no residual error).",
      "Dotted lines: the 15-20 mg/L trough range used in McCarthy 2026 Methods."
    )
  )
```

The paper does not tabulate simulated concentrations, so the profiles are
shown for orientation.

# PKNCA validation

At steady state the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL for every
patient. PKNCA's AUC over the simulated interval, divided by each patient's
`dose / cl`, should be 1 up to trapezoidal error on the 0.05-0.1 h grid.
McCarthy 2026 reports no NCA values, so there is no published table to compare
against.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- sim |>
  distinct(id, treatment, dose, tau) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = dose)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(treatment = unique(sim$treatment[sim$tau == 6]), start = 0, end = 6),
  data.frame(treatment = unique(sim$treatment[sim$tau == 8]), start = 0, end = 8)
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

cl_ind <- sim |> distinct(treatment, id, cl, dose, tau)
mass <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(cl_ind, by = c("treatment", "id")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / (dose / cl) - 1))
# Four model-cohort groups of 200 patients.
stopifnot(nrow(mass) == 800L, !anyNA(mass$pct_diff))
# The two sides use the same drawn parameters, so the difference is numerical
# (trapezoidal) error only.
stopifnot(max(abs(mass$pct_diff)) < 1)

mass |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    `Cmax (mg/L)` = median(cmax), `Cmin (mg/L)` = median(cmin),
    `AUCtau (mg*h/L)` = median(auclast), `AUC24 (mg*h/L)` = median(auclast * 24 / tau),
    `max abs(AUCtau vs dose/CL) (%)` = max(abs(pct_diff)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(`Model: cohort` = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA steady-state results (medians) and the dose/CL mass-balance check.")
```

```{r cvicu-ratio, include = FALSE}
auc24_med <- mass |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(auc24 = median(auclast * 24 / tau), .groups = "drop")
cvicu_ratio <- auc24_med$auc24[auc24_med$treatment == "Shimamoto refit: CVICU"] /
  auc24_med$auc24[auc24_med$treatment == "Moffett refit: CVICU"]
```

For the same CVICU cohort the two refits predict different exposure: the
median AUC24 of the Shimamoto refit is `r round(cvicu_ratio, 2)` times that of
the Moffett refit. The Shimamoto refit has a small central volume (12.7 L per
70 kg, hence the high peaks) and a lower typical clearance across the age range,
partly because its creatinine clearance uses Schwartz coefficients of
0.244-0.296 below 12 years, where the Moffett refit uses 0.413 at every age.
Both were fitted to the same patients; McCarthy 2026 judged them by
predictive performance (Fig. 3), not by agreement with each other.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Refit models, not the published originals.** These files hold the
  McCarthy 2026 re-estimates. The original Colin 2019, Moffett 2019 and
  Shimamoto 2024 models are separate publications; their estimates appear here
  only as the comparison in "Refit against published estimates".
- **Control stream over Table S2.** Where Table S2's printed equations differ
  from the refit control streams, the control streams were followed, because
  they are what was estimated: Table S2 writes the Colin maturation in weeks,
  while the stream (and its fixed `MAT50 = exp(-0.113)`) works in years, as a
  comment in the stream explains; Table S2 drops the `CANC` indicator from the
  Colin cancer term and prints the Shimamoto maturation denominator as
  `thetaPMA50 + PMA^Hill` rather than `T50^Hill + PMA^Hill`.
- **Colin heel-prick terms omitted.** The Colin stream carries heel-prick
  effects on V1 and Q (fixed at the Colin 2019 values), but McCarthy 2026 set
  heel-prick status to 0 for every patient (Table 2 footnote a), so both
  factors are 1 and the terms are left out. They are documented under
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Colin standardised creatinine.** The stream uses `LOG10` of PMA in years in
  `LnSCRstd`; this gives 0.831 mg/dL at the reference age, which matches the
  stream's comment of 0.84 mg/dL. The model reproduces the stream exactly.
- **Creatinine clearance equations.** Table 2 footnotes say Moffett uses the
  original Schwartz equation and Shimamoto the bedside one. The control streams
  instead use `0.413 * HT / CR` for Moffett and age-banded coefficients (0.244,
  0.277, 0.296, 0.413) for Shimamoto. The models follow the streams. Supply
  height in cm and creatinine in mg/dL.
- **AUC compartments dropped.** The Moffett and Shimamoto streams integrate an
  extra AUC state with no effect on the PK; it is omitted, and AUC comes from
  PKNCA instead.
- **Moffett additive error.** The stream fixes the additive SD at 0.0001 mg/L,
  a numerical floor, so the model is effectively proportional-only. Table 5
  lists only the proportional term.
- **Table 1 dose units.** Table 1 labels the dose row "mg/kg", but its values
  (median 428 mg in the oncology patients, up to 2500) are clearly in mg. The
  15 mg/kg dosing above reproduces those medians.
- **Virtual cohorts.** Weight and height come from approximate growth medians,
  not from the study data; creatinine is drawn without an age trend; and PMA is
  age plus 40 weeks for every child. These choices affect only the illustrative
  simulations, not the models.
- **Treatment courses.** Each treatment course was a separate individual in
  the refits, so the IIV describes variability between courses as well as
  between patients.
- No erratum or correction notice for McCarthy 2026 was found as of
  2026-11-12.
